brief: Conduct a legal audit on the PodBrain podcast knowledge base app — a React+Supabase web app that downloads podcast audio, transcribes it via OpenAI Whisper, generates embeddings and AI insights, and provides RAG-based chat. Currently personal-use, planning to productize. No auth, no legal pages, no compliance infrastructure exists.

roles.title: Privacy & Data Protection Counsel
roles.mission: Identify all personal data flows, assess GDPR/CCPA exposure, and produce a compliance gap analysis with remediation priorities.
roles.expertise: Data protection law (GDPR, CCPA, ePrivacy), privacy by design, data processing agreements, consent mechanisms, data retention policies.

roles.title: Intellectual Property & Content Rights Analyst
roles.mission: Assess copyright risks of downloading, transcribing, and storing podcast content, and evaluate fair use / licensing obligations.
roles.expertise: Copyright law, fair use doctrine, DMCA, content licensing, derivative works, podcast RSS legal norms, audio transcription IP issues.

roles.title: Third-Party API Compliance Analyst
roles.mission: Audit compliance with every third-party service's Terms of Service and acceptable use policies, flag violations and risks.
roles.expertise: SaaS terms of service analysis, API usage policies, data processing agreements, service-level agreements, acceptable use enforcement.

roles.title: Security & Access Control Auditor
roles.mission: Assess the app's security posture from a legal liability perspective — unauthorized access risks, data exposure, and duty-of-care gaps.
roles.expertise: Application security review, RLS policies, authentication/authorization, data exposure risk, breach liability, security disclosure obligations.

roles.title: Legal Policy Drafter
roles.mission: Synthesize findings from all other roles and draft actionable legal policy documents (Privacy Policy, Terms of Service) tailored to this app.
roles.expertise: Legal document drafting, privacy policy authoring, terms of service composition, plain-language legal writing, web app legal requirements.

tasks.title: Privacy & Data Flow Audit
tasks.prompt:
Conduct a comprehensive privacy and data protection audit of the PodBrain podcast app.

Context from reconnaissance:
- No authentication system (Supabase Auth planned but not implemented)
- No privacy policy, no cookie consent, no GDPR/CCPA compliance
- Data collected: knowledge base names, podcast URLs, full transcripts, chat conversations, search queries (stored in search_history table), AI-generated insights
- Data sent to third parties: OpenAI (audio for Whisper transcription, text for embeddings/GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini), Groq (audio + text), Podcast Index (search queries), Cobalt/Railway (YouTube URLs), Google Fonts CDN (IP addresses)
- All data stored indefinitely in Supabase Postgres — no retention policies, no deletion mechanisms
- No user data export capability
- Google Fonts loaded from CDN (transfers IP addresses to Google)
- Frontend exposes Supabase anon key (by design, safe per Supabase docs)

Deliver a structured report with:
1. Data inventory — every category of personal/user data collected, where it's stored, how long
2. Third-party data transfers — what data goes where, legal basis needed
3. GDPR gap analysis (assuming EU users are possible) — which articles are violated
4. CCPA gap analysis (assuming California users are possible)
5. ePrivacy / cookie compliance assessment
6. Risk matrix: each gap rated HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW with rationale
7. Prioritized remediation checklist (what to fix before going public)

Format: Markdown with clear headers, tables where appropriate. Length: 800-1200 words.

tasks.title: IP & Content Rights Assessment
tasks.prompt:
Assess the intellectual property and content rights risks of the PodBrain podcast app.

Context from reconnaissance:
- App downloads podcast audio from RSS feeds (via Podcast Index enclosure URLs) and YouTube (via Cobalt)
- Audio is temporarily stored in Supabase Storage during processing, then deleted after transcription
- Full transcripts are stored permanently in the database
- Transcripts are chunked, embedded (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small), and stored permanently
- GPT-4o generates derivative insights: summaries, topics, key points, entities — stored permanently
- Users can search across transcripts and chat with podcast content via RAG
- No attribution to original podcast creators in the UI beyond show name and episode title
- No copyright notices on the site
- No LICENSE file in the project
- Currently personal use, planning to productize with multi-user support

Deliver a structured report with:
1. Copyright analysis — who owns podcast audio, transcripts, and derivative insights?
2. Fair use assessment — does personal transcription + AI analysis qualify? What changes when productized?
3. RSS feed legal norms — what does publishing an RSS feed implicitly license?
4. YouTube/Cobalt risks — legal exposure from extracting YouTube audio
5. Derivative works analysis — are AI-generated summaries/insights derivative works?
6. DMCA considerations — what obligations arise if hosting user-contributed content?
7. Recommended protections: attribution requirements, takedown procedures, licensing terms
8. Risk matrix: each issue rated HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW

Format: Markdown with clear headers. Length: 800-1200 words.

tasks.title: Third-Party API TOS Compliance Audit
tasks.prompt:
Audit the PodBrain podcast app's compliance with every third-party service's Terms of Service.

Services used (from reconnaissance):

1. **OpenAI API** — Whisper (audio transcription), text-embedding-3-small (embeddings), GPT-4o (insight generation), GPT-4o-mini (RAG chat). App sends full podcast audio and transcript text to OpenAI.
2. **Groq API** — Alternative provider: Whisper-Large-v3 (transcription), Llama-3.3-70B (insights/chat). Same data as OpenAI.
3. **Podcast Index API** — Free, open podcast directory. Used for show search and episode listing. Auth via SHA-1 hash of key+secret+timestamp.
4. **Cobalt (self-hosted on Railway)** — YouTube audio extraction. Self-hosted instance of open-source tool. Sends YouTube URLs, receives audio streams.
5. **Supabase** — Database (Postgres + pgvector), Storage (temporary audio), Edge Functions (server-side processing). Stores all app data.
6. **Vercel** — Frontend hosting, auto-deploy from GitHub.
7. **Google Fonts CDN** — Font loading (Geist, Newsreader, JetBrains Mono). Implicit IP transfer.
8. **YouTube (via Cobalt)** — Audio extraction from YouTube videos as fallback source.

For EACH service, deliver:
- Summary of relevant TOS provisions (data usage, acceptable use, redistribution)
- Current compliance status (COMPLIANT / AT RISK / VIOLATION)
- Specific violations or risks identified
- What changes when the app goes from personal to commercial/multi-user
- Remediation steps if non-compliant

Pay special attention to:
- OpenAI's policy on storing/redistributing API outputs
- YouTube TOS on automated audio extraction
- Podcast Index acceptable use
- Whether commercial use changes any compliance status

Format: Markdown with a table per service. Length: 800-1200 words.

tasks.title: Security & Access Control Liability Audit
tasks.prompt:
Audit the PodBrain podcast app's security posture from a legal liability perspective.

Context from reconnaissance:
- NO authentication system — the app is completely open. Anyone with the URL can access all data.
- Supabase anon key is exposed in frontend .env (by Supabase design, but means anyone can query the database)
- NO Row-Level Security (RLS) policies enforced — all data accessible to anon role
- API keys (OpenAI, Groq, Podcast Index) are stored as Supabase secrets — server-side only, NOT exposed to frontend
- Edge Functions handle all sensitive API calls server-side
- Supabase Storage bucket 'podcast-audio' has RLS allowing anon INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE
- No rate limiting on any endpoints
- No input validation/sanitization visible in frontend code
- No security.txt or vulnerability disclosure policy
- No logging of access attempts or security events
- Currently deployed on Vercel (frontend) with Supabase backend
- CORS configured on Edge Functions

Deliver a structured report with:
1. Authentication & authorization gaps — legal exposure from no auth
2. Data exposure assessment — what can an unauthorized user access right now?
3. API key security review — are keys properly protected?
4. Storage bucket security — risks of open anon access
5. Input validation gaps — injection/XSS risks and liability
6. Breach notification obligations — what applies if data is exposed?
7. Duty of care analysis — what standard of security is legally expected?
8. Risk matrix: each finding rated CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
9. Prioritized remediation checklist for pre-launch security

Format: Markdown with clear headers and risk ratings. Length: 800-1200 words.

tasks.title: Draft Privacy Policy
tasks.prompt:
Draft a comprehensive Privacy Policy for the PodBrain podcast knowledge base app, suitable for a web application that will transition from personal use to a public product.

App details:
- Name: PodBrain
- Operator: Nick Lasky (individual, not a company entity yet)
- Contact email: nl.nicklasky@gmail.com
- What it does: Users create knowledge bases, add podcasts, the system transcribes audio and generates AI insights, users can search and chat with podcast content

Data collected:
- Knowledge base names and descriptions
- Podcast URLs, titles, show names
- Full podcast transcripts (generated from audio)
- AI-generated insights (summaries, topics, key points, entities)
- Chat conversations (user questions + AI answers with source citations)
- Search queries and search history
- Standard web data (IP addresses via hosting/CDN)

Third-party data processors:
- OpenAI (audio transcription via Whisper, text embeddings, GPT-4o insight generation, GPT-4o-mini chat)
- Groq (alternative transcription and AI processing)
- Supabase (database hosting, file storage, edge computing)
- Vercel (web hosting)
- Google Fonts (font delivery — transfers IP addresses)
- Podcast Index (podcast discovery API)

Requirements:
- Must cover GDPR basics (lawful basis, data subject rights, international transfers)
- Must cover CCPA basics (right to know, delete, opt-out)
- Plain language, not legalese
- Include sections: what we collect, how we use it, third-party sharing, data retention, your rights, security, children's privacy, changes to policy, contact
- Include effective date placeholder
- Note: this is a DRAFT for legal review, not final legal advice

Format: Ready-to-publish Markdown. Length: 1000-1500 words. Add a disclaimer header that this is a draft requiring attorney review.

App details:

- Operator: Nick Lasky (individual, not a company entity yet)
- Contact email: nl.nicklasky@gmail.com
